description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of different entity types identified in a biomedical named entity recognition task, with each slice corresponding to a specific category and its proportional share. The chart is divided into 20 distinct segments, each labeled with its category name and percentage value. The largest segment is “Chemical,” occupying 32% of the pie and colored blue. The second largest is “Protein” at 15%, shown in orange. “DNA” accounts for 6% and is green. Several categories share equal proportions: “Chemical Family,” “Disease,” and “Cell Type” each represent 5% and are colored red, purple, and brown respectively. “Drug” is 4% and pink, while “Frequency,” “Cell Line,” and “Dosage” each make up 3% and are gray, yellow, and cyan respectively. Categories such as “Form,” “Gene Or Gene Product,” “Strength,” “Specific Disease,” “Route,” “Reason,” “Chemical Entity,” “Modifier,” “RNA,” “Disease Class,” “Organism Taxon,” “Duration,” “ADE,” and “Composite Mention” each represent 2% or 1% of the total, with their respective colors including orange, blue, green, red, purple, brown, pink, gray, yellow, cyan, and various other hues. The chart includes percentage labels directly within each slice and does not use a separate legend; the categories are labeled directly adjacent to their corresponding slices. The segments are arranged in descending order of size, starting with “Chemical” at the top and proceeding clockwise to the smallest segments on the right.
